newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese medicine maker seeks listing in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Chinese medicine maker seeks listing in Hong Kong.

text.p: Chinese medicine maker Sanjiu Group plans to raise 700 million yuan (US$84.3 million) by listing its Shenzhen joint venture in Hong Kong, the Hongkong Standard reported on Friday.

The group, owned by the Chinese People's Liberation Army, would use proceeds from the listing of Shenzhen 999 Pharmaceutical Co to develop new products aimed at increasing sales by 50 percent, the newspaper reported.

New lines of medicine, to treat arthritis and cancer, were expected to boost sales of the joint venture to three billion yuan by 1998 from two billion yuan in 1995, the newspaper quoted a company official as saying.
The group hopes to receive approval for the listing in November and flotation is planned for mid-1997, it reported.
"Due to the nature of our company, we have a special relationship with central authorities and we expect the plan to be approved," the newspaper quoted a company official as saying.
The company was not immediately available for comment. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
